long_biography.plain_text:
A change-of-control approval in 2000 placed Aristotle Halikias, Patricia Halikias and Terry Halikias in control of Republic Bank of Chicago. Aristotle became board chairman and helped oversee expansion, including purchases of failed institutions. The approval identified joint family acquisition but supplied no individual percentage or evidence that the bank's assets belong to him personally.

Real estate had already shaped his career. After earlier Illinois banking appointments, Halikias became president and chief executive of Intercontinental Real Estate and Development in 1994. He later chaired a listed Greek property company whose portfolio moved into BriQ Properties. He owns one third of Ajolico, which holds a material BriQ block, while reporting no direct BriQ shares or indirect voting rights. He remains a non-executive BriQ director. These facts establish active operating and investment roles, but they do not reveal whether banking, property, inheritance or personally earned capital contributes most to his wealth.

uncertainties: Official Greek filings use Panagiotis-Aristeidis Halikias, often transliterated Aristides or Aristidis Halikias. English institutional sources use Aristotle P. Halikias. The Greek name, Republic Bank and ICRED roles, Chicago residence and birth year establish that these are the same person; Peter is retained as the established English expansion of the public middle initial.

The owner record's sort_name says Aristotle Michael Halikias. Greek filings say Panagiotis-Aristeidis 'of Michael,' identifying a patronymic rather than a middle name. The sort name is therefore proposed for correction to Aristotle Peter Halikias.

A current official filing identifies Toronto, Canada, as his birthplace and Greek as his citizenship. The existing Greece birth country is proposed for correction; Canadian nationality is not inferred from birthplace and remains unresolved.

The owner record stores '1961' in birth_day, which cannot be a valid calendar day and is evidently a displaced year. Two official filings confirm 1961 as the birth year. Only a low-tier aggregator gives 1 April 1961, so day 1 remains a 72-confidence candidate and the malformed existing day should be cleared only through explicit review.

Illinois regulators approved Aristotle, Patricia and Terry Halikias to acquire control of Republic Bank in 2000. The record does not disclose their individual percentages, acquisition funding or whether any earlier family transfer contributed capital.
The bank describes itself as family-owned, but its deposits, loans, regulatory assets and branch network belong to the institution. They are not treated as Halikias's personal property or net worth.

BriQ's report says Halikias owns 33.3 per cent of Ajolico, which in turn held 14.46 per cent of BriQ at year-end 2024. It also says he held no direct BriQ shares, claimed no indirect voting rights and did not singly control Ajolico. BriQ's total portfolio and market value are therefore not attributed to him.

Halikias is documented as president and chief executive of ICRED, but no reliable public source located in this research discloses his ownership percentage in that private company. ICRED project values remain corporate rather than personal assets.

Real Estate is the strongest candidate for both industry fields because of the long ICRED role and Ajolico interest. Banking is also a plausible current primary sector because of family bank control, so neither industry clears 85 without comparative personal asset evidence.

Self-made is plausible from the long executive career and joint bank acquisition, but the funding source and potential family transfers are not public. Inheritance is not assigned merely from family ownership.

Operator is plausible from the continuing chairman and chief-executive roles, while Investor is supported by Ajolico. The principal relationship remains Unknown because the dominant personal asset cannot be identified.

Focused exact-name searches found no dedicated Forbes profile or verified Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website. The LinkedIn profile and current BriQ company biography are proposed.
